items.title: From Juddha Shumsher’s speech to Malla-era manuscripts, 800 historical documents return to Nepal

items.desc: Police will step up patrols and surveillance in crowded and sensitive areas, using CCTV cameras, drones and sniffer dogs to prevent theft, robbery and other festival-related crimes.

items.desc: The Post spoke to 12 children from the flood-affected areas and gathered their experiences and the nightmares that still follow them.

items.title: Floods drive 33 pregnant women to Kathmandu for childbirth
items.desc: Local maternity clinics and services remain disrupted in Rasuwa and Nuwakot since the August 26 floods. But many women cannot travel to Kathmandu because of damaged roads.

items.desc: Kushal Bhurtel misses head coach Stuart Law’s 15-member travelling squad to Oman, where the tri-series kicks off on October 7.

items.title: Can new rules bring order to senior advocate selection?
items.desc: A special committee will review past appointments and develop clearer criteria based on lawyers’ professional performance and contribution.

items.title: Nine things to know about the rape case at Cornell University
items.desc: A former Cornell student’s allegations against seven men have reopened a criminal investigation nearly two years after the alleged assault at a fraternity house.

items.title: Israeli passenger says he knew what to do on flydubai plane after watching TV show
items.desc: A passenger who helped subdue a co-pilot after the captain was stabbed says an air-crash TV show taught him how to pull the plane out of a nose dive.

items.title: Scrub typhus claims nine lives in Salyan in six weeks
items.desc: Nearly 600 people have tested positive as the disease spreads to eight local units, prompting a central health investigation.

items.title: Why Deuba should stop the circus

items.title: Nepali teachers have found their way to AI. Can our education system keep up?
items.desc: When teachers are prepared and properly supported, AI can become a valuable professional partner, one whose answers they examine rather than accept.

items.title: Nepal must turn satellite observations into early warnings
items.desc: If scientists can detect potentially significant deformation after an event, why is there no operational system routinely monitoring for similar changes before disaster strikes?

items.title: Federal Civil Service Bill reaches parliament, ten years after federalism
items.desc: Bill proposes new administrative structure, retirement rules, recruitment quotas, lateral entry, and a two-year cooling-off period, among other things.

items.title: Congress factions clash over party’s socialist path
items.desc: The debate centres on how the grand old party should adapt BP Koirala’s socialist principles to changing political and economic realities.

items.title: China proposes upgrading Korala as international trading point as Nepal insists on Tatopani reopening
items.desc: Nepali authorities have requested the Chinese side to reopen Tatopani urgently to allow for merchandise from the north to reach Kathmandu for the festivals.

items.title: Army chief Sigdel to visit UK on seven-day official trip
items.desc: The visit will be his first to Britain since he became Nepal’s army chief in September 2024.

items.title: Nepal’s track and field athletes train for the Asian Para Games on their own terms
items.desc: The Post profiles the members of Nepal’s athletics squad who are training without state sponsorship, adapting to disabilities, financial hardship and personal tragedies as they prepare for the Asian Para Games in Nagoya.

items.title: How Anup Poudel took Nepali cinema to Cannes
items.desc: Poudel’s journey from a movie-goer in Kavre to an award-winning producer reflects the growing global reach of Nepali independent cinema.

items.title: Eight more bodies recovered from Himlung avalanche as death toll reaches 15
items.desc: The victims were among 16 Nepali workers and support staff preparing routes and camps ahead of foreign climbers when the avalanche struck the 7,126-metre peak on September 26.

items.title: Kathmandu Climate Week to begin Friday with focus on climate justice
items.desc: Organisers say the programme will address climate-finance bottlenecks, data gaps and structural barriers that keep support from reaching the most exposed communities.

items.title: Foreign Minister Khanal to attend Pre-COP leaders’ event in Fiji, visit Australia
items.desc: Khanal will deliver remarks at the leaders’ plenary in Fiji and meet Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong in Canberra on October 8.

items.title: Floods disrupt livelihoods of 21,400 workers in Nepal: ILO
items.desc: The UN agency says damage to homes, workplaces, roads, bridges and energy infrastructure could spread employment and income losses far beyond flood-hit areas.

items.title: ADB backs Nepal power transmission, battery storage projects through PPPs
items.desc: The agreements will support a 134-kilometre, 400-kilovolt transmission line and 100–150 megawatt-hours of utility-scale battery storage, with the projects expected to mobilise more than $200 million in private investment.

items.title: Domestic Airline Liability Bill set for Friday passage, proposes $100,000 passenger compensation
items.desc: The bill, unanimously endorsed by a parliamentary committee and tabled in the National Assembly on Thursday, seeks to overhaul insurance provisions in Nepal’s domestic airline industry.

items.title: State-run food company to skip goat sales this Dashain
items.desc: The company says repeated losses and transport disruptions have made goat trading too risky; it is selling sugar Rs16 a kg below market prices and raising the purchase limit to 25 kg per customer.

items.title: Nepal’s new federal civil service bill, explained in nine points
items.desc: The bill would change some existing rules, retain others and introduce new provisions covering recruitment, pensions, retirement, inclusion and federal, provincial and local administration .
